HYPOTHESIS: Inventory growth is most likely to be unproductive when firms simultaneously have weak gross profitability and a thin working-capital cushion.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Prior evidence favored inventory investment conditioned on either weak margins or strained liquidity; this combines those economically distinct quality filters without using a mechanically linked sales-to-inventory ratio. High values identify inventory build that is both low-margin and liquidity-stressed, a more targeted overhang signal than inventory growth alone.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

NAME: LowMarginInventoryAcceleration
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(invt, at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: A sudden acceleration in inventory intensity predicts weaker returns when gross profitability is poor.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This shifts the investment leg from inventory growth level to an inventory ramp, targeting abrupt overproduction or demand miscalibration. Pairing the ramp with low gross profitability keeps the mechanism focused on low-quality working-capital expansion rather than normal inventory rebuilding.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: LowMarginCapexAcceleration
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(capx, at))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Capex acceleration is most concerning when firms have persistently weak gross profitability.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive suggests capex acceleration is more informative than capex level, so this tests whether margin quality is a stronger conditioning state than cash-flow quality. A rapid capital-spending ramp by low-margin firms is more likely to reflect competitive pressure or overexpansion than disciplined investment.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: IssuanceFundedLossCashHoard
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ib, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash accumulation predicts weaker returns when it is equity-financed by unprofitable firms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The prior loss-firm cash-build signal had weak portfolio evidence, so this version isolates the adverse-selection channel more directly by requiring equity issuance alongside the cash build. High values capture firms raising capital and parking it as cash despite poor earnings, consistent with survival financing rather than productive investment capacity.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: EquityFundedWeakIntangibleBuild
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(intan, 1), at)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible-asset expansion is more likely to be low quality when financed by equity issuance at firms with weak operating cash flow.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Intangible growth can reflect valuable investment, but it is harder to verify and more vulnerable to overpayment or capitalization concerns. Combining intangible build with equity issuance and weak internal cash generation targets externally financed, low-discipline expansion rather than all intangible investment.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: LowMarginHiringExpansion
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(emp, 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Employment growth predicts weaker returns when firms lack gross-profitability support.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Hiring is a real investment in operating capacity, but at low-margin firms it can indicate cost bloat or inefficient scaling. This differs from sales-confirmation hiring tests by conditioning labor expansion on product-market profitability rather than contemporaneous demand growth.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE DualWeakInventoryBuild---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially an arithmetic blend of two archive signals (LowMarginInventoryBuild, fmb_tstat -4.47, and the much weaker LiquidityStrainedInventoryBuild, fmb_tstat -1.19) with the identical inventory-growth leg, so it is a cosmetic averaging that most likely dilutes the stronger margin conditioner rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE LowMarginInventoryAcceleration---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Replacing inventory growth with an inventory-intensity ramp is a genuine change to the investment leg motivated by the archive's finding that ACCEL improved the capex family (ls_talpha -3.95 vs -2.21), though the low-gross-profitability leg means part of any result will simply reload on the Novy-Marx profitability anomaly.

---CRITIQUE LowMarginCapexAcceleration---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is CashWeakCapexAcceleration with only the conditioning variable swapped from cash-flow quality to gross margin — an incremental one-leg substitution rather than the substantively different construction the objective calls for, and the substituted leg is itself a well-known standalone anomaly.

---CRITIQUE IssuanceFundedLossCashHoard---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The three-way rank product is dominated by the joint tail and, more importantly, the two active components (share issuance and low profitability) are among the most heavily documented published anomalies, so a negative result would largely be a rediscovery rather than evidence for the cash-hoarding channel.

---CRITIQUE EquityFundedWeakIntangibleBuild---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The intangible-build leg is the least-explored component and the hypothesis matches the expression's direction, but the triple rank product will thin an already low-coverage sample (LowProfitIntangibleBuild was 0.117) and overlaps meaningfully with the archived ExternallyFundedCashFlowWeakExpansion, so it needs to beat that benchmark rather than merely be significant.

---CRITIQUE LowMarginHiringExpansion---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: A plain product of two published anomalies — the hiring-rate/employment-growth effect (Belo-Lin-Bazdresch) and reversed gross profitability (Novy-Marx) — with no conditioning structure beyond their interaction, and the archive's two prior hiring conditionings both failed (fmb_tstat 0.05 and -1.64), making this both derivative and unpromising.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: MarginDecayInventoryBuild
EXPRESSION: SUB(MUL(RANK(GROWTH(invt, 1)), INDICATOR(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 3)), 0)), MUL(RANK(GROWTH(invt, 1)), INDICATOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 3), 0)))
HYPOTHESIS: Inventory growth is harmful when gross margins are deteriorating, but less concerning when margin trends confirm healthy demand.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This replaces the prior arithmetic blend of inventory-quality signals with an explicit conditional contrast. The mechanism is not simply “inventory plus weak quality,” but inventory accumulation specifically when product-market economics are worsening.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CashWeakUnderMaintenance
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(capx, dp), at))), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Low net capital investment is a negative signal when it occurs alongside deteriorating operating cash-flow quality.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This moves away from another capex-acceleration conditioner swap and tests a different mechanism: under-maintenance rather than overexpansion. Low investment is not treated as generically good; it becomes problematic when weak cash generation suggests firms may be deferring necessary reinvestment.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: NonOperatingCashBuildMarginDecay
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MIN(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(che, 1), oancf), at))), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash accumulation predicts weaker returns when the cash build is not supported by operating cash flow and margins are deteriorating.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This removes the dominant share-issuance and low-profitability legs and focuses directly on the cash-hoarding channel. The MIN construction requires both a cash build and a cash build in excess of operating cash generation, while the margin-decay condition distinguishes precautionary or nonproductive liquidity from cash generated by strong operations.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: DeterioratingROEGoodwillBuild
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(gdwl, 1), at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(ni, ceq), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Goodwill accumulation is more likely to reflect overpayment or low-quality acquired growth when return on equity is deteriorating.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This abandons the weak hiring-growth channel rather than forcing another derivative hiring interaction. Goodwill build is a distinct investment channel tied to acquisition premiums, and deteriorating ROE provides a post-investment quality test of whether that expansion is translating into shareholder productivity.
